name: Elasticsearch
description: The Elasticsearch app is a unified logs and metrics app that helps you monitor the availability, performance, health and resource utilization of your Elasticsearch clusters. Preconfigured dashboards provide insight into cluster health, resource utilization, sharding, garbage collection, and search, index and cache performance.

children.name: Elasticsearch - Garbage Collection
children.description: The Elasticsearch - Garbage Collector dashboard provides information on the garbage collection of the Java Virtual Machine.
children.title: Elasticsearch - Garbage Collection

queries.queryString:
db_cluster=* db_system=elasticsearch db_cluster={{db_cluster}} "Pre Evacuate Collection Set" or "Merge Heap Roots" or "Evacuate Collection Set" or "Post Evacuate Collection Set" or "Other" | json "log" as rawlog nodrop
| if (isEmpty(_rawlog), raw, rawlog) as raw 
| parse regex "\[(?<date>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<process_id>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<module>[^\]]+)\]\s+GC\(.*\)(?<Time_Name>.*):\s+(?<pre_collect_set>\d+\.\d+)ms"
| timeslice by 1h 
| if (isEmpty(pod),_sourceHost,pod) as host
| count(process_id) as Total_Process_Id group by Time_Name

db_cluster=* db_system=elasticsearch db_cluster={{db_cluster}} "Pre Evacuate Collection Set" or "Merge Heap Roots" or "Evacuate Collection Set" or "Post Evacuate Collection Set" or "Other" | json "log" as rawlog nodrop
| if (isEmpty(_rawlog), raw, rawlog) as raw
| parse regex "\[(?<date>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<process_id>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<module>[^\]]+)\]\s+GC\(.*\)(?<Time_Name>.*):\s+(?<pre_collect_set>\d+\.\d+)ms"
| timeslice by 1h 
| if (isEmpty(pod),_sourceHost,pod) as host
| sum(pre_collect_set) as Total_Pre_Collect group by Time_Name

db_cluster=* db_system=elasticsearch db_cluster={{db_cluster}} "Pre Evacuate Collection Set" or "Merge Heap Roots" or "Evacuate Collection Set" or "Post Evacuate Collection Set" or "Other" | json "log" as rawlog nodrop
| if (isEmpty(_rawlog), raw, rawlog) as raw 
| parse regex "\[(?<date>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<process_id>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<module>[^\]]+)\]\s+GC\(.*\)(?<Time_Name>.*):\s+(?<pre_collect_set>\d+\.\d+)ms"
| timeslice by 1h 
| if (isEmpty(pod),_sourceHost,pod) as host
| avg(pre_collect_set) as Avg_Pre_Collect group by Time_Name

db_cluster=* db_system=elasticsearch db_cluster={{db_cluster}} | json "log" as _rawlog nodrop 
| if (isEmpty(_rawlog), _raw, _rawlog) as mesg
| parse regex field=mesg "\[(?<date>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<process_id>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<module>[^\]]+)\].*(?<HeapBfrGC>\d+)M->(?<HeapAftrGC>\d+)M\((?<HeapSize>\d+)M\)\s+(?<GCOperationTime>[\d.]+)ms"
| timeslice 15m
| sum(GCOperationTime) as GCOperationTime by _timeslice

panels.title: GC - User Time

queries.queryString:
db_cluster=* db_system=elasticsearch db_cluster={{db_cluster}} | json "log" as _rawlog nodrop 
| if (isEmpty(_rawlog), _raw, _rawlog) as _raw
| parse regex "\[(?<date>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<process_id>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<module>[^\]]+)\]\s+GC\(.*\)\s*User=(?<user_time>\d+.\d+)s\s+Sys=(?<sys_time>\d+\.\d+)s\s+Real=(?<real_time>\d+.\d+)"
| avg(user_time) as Avg_User_Time, avg(sys_time) as Avg_Sys_Time, avg(real_time) as  Avg_Real_Time
| fields Avg_User_Time

queries.queryString: db_cluster=* metric=elasticsearch_indices_stats_total_translog_operations db_cluster={{db_cluster}} host={{host}} | sum by db_cluster,host

panels.title: Changes to Lucene are only persisted to disk during a Lucene commit, which is a relatively expensive operation and so cannot be performed after every index or delete operation. Changes that happen after one commit and before another will be removed from the index by Lucene in the event of process exit or hardware failure.  Lucene commits are too expensive to perform on every individual change, so each shard copy also writes operations into its transaction log known as the translog. All index and delete operations are written to the translog after being processed by the internal Lucene index but before they are acknowledged. In the event of a crash, recent operations that have been acknowledged but not yet included in the last Lucene commit are instead recovered from the translog when the shard recovers.

panels.description: A shard in Elasticsearch is a Lucene index, and a Lucene index is broken down into segments. Segments are internal storage elements in the index where the index data is stored, and are immutable. Smaller segments are periodically merged into larger segments to keep the index size at bay and to expunge deletes.
